overall: The AG found the Planning Board violated the Open Meeting Law: a quorum deliberated via serial communications about the Minimum Map, and the chair's talking-points email was improper deliberation. The Board was ordered to release emails and comply going forward.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged the Wakefield Planning Board deliberated outside a posted meeting about the Minimum Map by serial emails and calls among members before Spring Town Meeting.
allegations.key_passage: The information before us, therefore, confirms that a quorum discussed through separate, serial communication a plan to introduce the Minimum Map at Spring Town Meeting as an alternative to the Original Overlay District.

allegations.summary: Chair's emailed 'talking points' attachment, sent to three other members before Spring Town Meeting, was alleged to be deliberation outside a posted meeting.
allegations.key_passage: Chair Noell’s distribution of the “talking points” document also constituted improper deliberation.

remedy: Publicly release within 30 days of receipt all emails from any Board member to other Board member(s) referencing the Minimum Map and/or plans to amend Article 17 prior to Spring Town Meeting, to the extent not already released.
Immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law's requirements; future similar violations may be considered evidence of intent to violate the law.
remedy_passage: We order the Board to publicly release within 30 days of receipt of this determination all emails from any Board member to one or more other Board member(s) which reference the Minimum Map and /or plans to amend Article 17 prior to Spring Town Meeting, to the extent it has not already done so.
